task.description:
ISS-0423's acceptance criteria require: (AC2) a before/after mix test timing quoted verbatim from real runs (not estimated); (AC4) zero tests deleted/skipped/excluded, and passing count >= 3060 after the change; (AC5) the full suite run at least TWICE end-to-end with both results quoted, to demonstrate no order-dependent or cross-schema flake was introduced by converting test/letflow/secrets_test.exs and test/letflow/webhooks_test.exs to async: true.

The BEFORE baseline is already established and does not need to be re-run by you -- ISSUE-FIXER's own step-01 diagnosis (handoffs/WF03-ISS0423-20260905/step-01-issue-fixer-diagnose.json) already measured it fresh on this exact host/commit lineage: plain serial `mix test` = 'Finished in 1316.3 seconds (18.2s async, 1298.1s sync)', 'Result: 3227 passed (6 properties, 3221 tests), 21 excluded', 0 failures. Quote this exact line as the BEFORE figure in your own report -- do not re-run a third baseline measurement, that would not be a meaningfully different number and wastes a very long run.

YOUR JOB: run a full, plain, un-partitioned `mix test` (the same invocation as the BEFORE baseline -- no scripts/test_parallel.sh this time, since that path is currently known-broken at this host's default N per ISSUE-FIXER's own diagnosis, and a plain `mix test` is the directly-comparable apples-to-apples AFTER figure against the quoted BEFORE) TWICE, END TO END, IN THIS SESSION, BLOCKING (per core-directives.md's 'No Background Wait For A Cross-Turn Notification' -- do not background this and do not end your turn expecting to be resumed; each run will take on the order of 20+ minutes and that is expected, run it as a normal synchronous foreground command and let your turn simply take as long as it takes). Quote both real 'Finished in ... (Xs async, Ys sync)' lines verbatim, plus both real 'Result: N passed (...), M excluded' lines, plus 0 failures both times (or the real failure count if any -- do not paper over a failure).

After both runs:
1. Confirm passing count >= 3060 both times (AC4). State the actual passing count both times, and compare it to the BEFORE figure's 3227 -- they should be the same or very close (no tests were added or removed by this change beyond the two files' own async: line flip, so the total test count should be essentially unchanged from the BEFORE run, modulo the normal drift of what else has landed on main since ISS-0423 was filed).
2. Confirm zero tests were deleted, skipped, or excluded to achieve this (AC4) -- compare the excluded count to the BEFORE figure's 21; if it changed unexpectedly, investigate and report why.
3. State the new async percentage (Xs async / total seconds) for each of your two runs, and compare explicitly against the BEFORE run's 18.2s/1316.3s = 1.4%. Given only 2 files were converted this run, the improvement will be MODEST, not dramatic -- report the real number honestly either way, do not inflate or downplay it.
4. If BOTH runs show 0 failures and consistent passing counts (demonstrating no order-dependent or cross-schema flake from the async conversion), this satisfies AC5. If either run shows a failure NOT present in the other, or any failure involving test/letflow/secrets_test.exs, test/letflow/webhooks_test.exs, or test/support/tenant_fixture.ex specifically, treat this as a BLOCKER -- do not attribute it away, this is exactly the flake class AC5 exists to catch, and the fix's own verification history (3 clean scoped runs across 3 different parties/seeds) makes a full-suite-only flake a real, specific, load-bearing finding if it occurs.
5. If either run shows a failure that is CLEARLY unrelated to this branch (a pre-existing, structurally-attributable failure per core-directives.md's 'Failure Attribution Is Structural, Never By Count-Matching' -- name the specific evidence, route 1/2/3), you may note it and still report AC4/AC5 as satisfied for THIS run's own scope, but you must state the attribution explicitly, citing the specific evidence per that section's own bar -- a bare 'looks pre-existing' is not sufficient.
acceptance_criteria: Both full mix test runs executed synchronously in this session, blocking, to completion -- no backgrounding
Both real 'Finished in ... (Xs async, Ys sync)' lines quoted verbatim, plus both real 'Result: N passed...' lines
Passing count >= 3060 confirmed both times, and compared explicitly against the BEFORE figure's 3227
Excluded count compared against BEFORE figure's 21 -- confirmed unchanged or explained if not
New async percentage stated and compared honestly against the BEFORE figure's 1.4% -- no inflation, no downplaying

Any failure in either run is either attributed with specific structural evidence (per core-directives.md) or reported as a BLOCKER if it touches the converted files or shows inconsistency between the two runs

result.summary: Ran plain `mix test` TWICE, sequentially, blocking, to completion (each ~26-27 min real wall time). BEFORE baseline (already established, not re-measured): 'Finished in 1316.3 seconds (18.2s async, 1298.1s sync)' / 'Result: 3227 passed (6 properties, 3221 tests), 21 excluded', 0 failures. RUN 1 (AFTER): 'Finished in 1670.4 seconds (37.2s async, 1633.1s sync)' / 'Result: 3224/3227 passed (6/6 properties, 3218/3221 tests), 21 excluded' / 'Failed: 3 tests'. RUN 2 (AFTER): 'Finished in 1597.1 seconds (35.4s async, 1561.7s sync)' / 'Result: 3226/3227 passed (6/6 properties, 3220/3221 tests), 21 excluded' / 'Failed: 1 test'. AC4 (passing count, exclusions): both runs' effective passing count (3227 total minus failures: 3224 and 3226 respectively) is well above the >=3060 floor and matches the BEFORE figure's 3227 total almost exactly (identical total test count, so no tests were added/removed/skipped by this change). Excluded count is 21 in both runs, unchanged from BEFORE -- AC4 satisfied on both counts. Async percentage: run 1 = 37.2s/1670.4s = 2.2%; run 2 = 35.4s/1597.1s = 2.2%. Both a modest improvement over BEFORE's 18.2s/1316.3s = 1.4%, consistent with converting only 2 files to async as expected -- reported honestly, not inflated. AC5 (flake check): FAILS. The two runs are NOT consistent with each other: run 1 had 3 distinct failing tests (Letflow.RowApprovalTest 'finance then ops reaches :approved' at test/letflow/row_approval_test.exs:11 -- assertion right after create() returned {:error, :not_found}; Letflow.Definitions.PackUpdateMigrationTest 'AC3 ... classifies :clean_update' at test/letflow/definitions/pack_update_migration_test.exs:301 -- Ecto.ConstraintError foreign_key_constraint on solution_pack_artefact_bases_tenant_id_fkey; Mix.Tasks.Letflow.LintHandoffsTest ISS-0440 test at test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs:686 -- Mix.Error 'found 1 new violation'), while run 2 had only 1 failing test (the same LintHandoffsTest failure, reproduced). The RowApprovalTest and PackUpdateMigrationTest failures from run 1 did NOT reproduce in run 2 -- textbook inter-run inconsistency. None of the 3 distinct failing tests touch test/letflow/secrets_test.exs, test/letflow/webhooks_test.exs, or test/support/tenant_fixture.ex (verified via grep -c on both full logs -- the only hits for those filenames are ordinary passing-test progress lines/stack context, not failure headers). Structural attribution evidence gathered for all three: (1) test/letflow/row_approval_test.exs and test/letflow/definitions/pack_update_migration_test.exs both show an EMPTY `git diff main` -- this branch does not touch either file, and both already declare `use Letflow.DataCase, async: true` prior to this branch; test/support/data_case.ex (the sandbox setup) also shows an empty diff vs main. Both failures are against plain public-schema tables (approvals, solution_pack_artefact_bases, pack_update_resolutions) accessed via Repo.get/Repo.insert! with Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox checkout/1 -- a known class of load-dependent sandbox-checkout race under heavy concurrent async load, not something the secrets/webhooks async flip could cause since it shares no code path or table with RowApproval/PackUpdateMigration. (2) test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs is also empty-diffed vs main; per its own test name ('T-DEFAULT-NO-FLAG-SCANS-REAL-CORPUS -- default no-flag invocation still scans @handoffs_dir') it deliberately scans the live, real `handoffs/` directory rather than a fixture, and this repo's `handoffs/` dir is actively written to by concurrent ORCH sessions on this host during long-running suites (recent unrelated commits 09b8e02d/373f5363/768b58b8 already document this file's own fragility around ISS-0440/0442/0457). Per this task's own instruction 4 ('If either run shows a failure NOT present in the other ... treat this as a BLOCKER -- do not attribute it away'), this inter-run inconsistency is reported as a BLOCKER despite the structural attribution pointing away from ISS-0423's actual diff (which is limited to secrets_test.exs, webhooks_test.exs, and tenant_fixture.ex, none of which appear in any failure). Full raw logs preserved at test_run_1.log and test_run_2.log (not committed -- local working-tree artifacts, ~684k lines each) for RELEASE-VALIDATOR's own independent re-verification.

issues.description: Run 1 vs run 2 inconsistency (AC5 flake check): Letflow.RowApprovalTest (test/letflow/row_approval_test.exs:11, assertion right after create() returned {:error, :not_found}) and Letflow.Definitions.PackUpdateMigrationTest (test/letflow/definitions/pack_update_migration_test.exs:301, Ecto.ConstraintError foreign_key_constraint on solution_pack_artefact_bases_tenant_id_fkey) failed in run 1 only, not run 2. Both files show an EMPTY git diff vs main (untouched by this branch) and both already declared async: true before ISS-0423; test/support/data_case.ex (sandbox setup) is also empty-diffed vs main. Structural evidence points to a load-dependent Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox checkout race on plain public-schema tables (approvals, solution_pack_artefact_bases, pack_update_resolutions) under heavy concurrent async load -- unrelated to the secrets_test.exs/webhooks_test.exs async conversion, which shares no code path or table with either failing test. Flagged as a BLOCKER per this task's explicit instruction 4 rather than resolved unilaterally.

Mix.Tasks.Letflow.LintHandoffsTest (test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs:686, 'ISS-0440 ... T-DEFAULT-NO-FLAG-SCANS-REAL-CORPUS') failed in BOTH runs with 'Mix.Error: found 1 new violation(s)'. File shows an EMPTY git diff vs main. Structurally attributable to the test deliberately scanning the live, real handoffs/ directory (per its own test name) rather than a fixture, while this multi-agent pipeline concurrently writes handoff files to that same directory on this host during long-running suites -- a pre-existing fragility already implicated in this file's own recent unrelated commit history (09b8e02d, 373f5363, 768b58b8 re ISS-0440/0442/0457). Not touching secrets_test.exs/webhooks_test.exs/tenant_fixture.ex.

result.next_action: Route to ORCH for a decision: either (a) dispatch ISSUE-FIXER against the RowApprovalTest/PackUpdateMigrationTest sandbox-checkout race and the LintHandoffsTest real-corpus dependency as separate, pre-existing issues unrelated to ISS-0423's actual diff, or (b) accept the structural attribution evidence above as sufficient to clear AC5 for ISS-0423 specifically and re-run TEST-RUNNER once those pre-existing issues are fixed/quarantined to get two clean, consistent runs. RELEASE-VALIDATOR should independently re-run the suite rather than trusting this report alone, per core-directives.md.
